mfg1-mechanical-lesson-057.title: Do not confuse protection against dust with protection against gas
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-057.objective: Check the protected hazard and the equipment’s suitability, and match clothing and eye protection to the process.

paragraphs.title: Particles and gases are different
paragraphs.text: A dust respirator is intended to filter particles such as dust. Do not assume it removes harmful gases in the same way. Gases require checking protective equipment suitable for the substance, while oxygen deficiency is a separate hazard. Ask the responsible person about the type, applicable conditions and fitting checks.

paragraphs.title: Match eye and body protection to the task
paragraphs.text: Protective glasses guard the eyes against flying material and similar hazards. Tasks such as gas cutting also require the specified protection against harmful light. Match sleeves and gloves to the process, observing prohibitions such as no gloves at a rotating drill press. Do not apply one example outfit to every task.

paragraphs.title: Check engineering measures too
paragraphs.text: Wearing protective equipment does not solve poor ventilation or a broken guard. When dust increases, withdraw to a safe position and report the source, ventilation, protective equipment and work conditions. Do not choose equipment of unknown protective performance merely by its color or shape.

terms.meaning: Measures against particles such as dust.
A gas that may damage health.
Reducing harmful light.
Wearing equipment in the specified position and manner.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-057.activity:
4 minutes: Check the goal and terms.
10 minutes: Read the text and organize the conditions and reasons for decisions.
7 minutes: Separate the facts in the example from what remains unconfirmed.
7 minutes: For dust, gas and cutting light, separately list the protected hazard and the performance that needs further checking.
2 minutes: Summarize the key points and what to confirm at work.
safety: Do not enter a place with unknown gas or suspected oxygen deficiency merely because you have a mask.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-057.summary: Particle, gas and light protection are different. Check the performance suitable for the process and substance.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-058.title: In a fire, prioritize reporting, evacuation and suitable initial action
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-058.objective: Distinguish what is burning and whether it is energized; do not independently begin dangerous firefighting.

paragraphs.title: Alert others first
paragraphs.text: On discovering fire or smoke, alert others through the workplace emergency procedure and secure a safe evacuation route. In normal conditions, check not only extinguisher locations but also whom to call, the assembly point and the conditions for evacuation. Do not return to investigate a place obscured by smoke.

paragraphs.title: Read the fire class and extinguisher suitability
paragraphs.text: The source describes ordinary fires involving wood or paper, oil fires and electrical fires as classes A, B and C. Applying water to oil or energized parts is dangerous. Read the extinguisher’s suitability marking rather than assuming every extinguishing agent suits every fire.

paragraphs.title: Stay within the permitted scope
paragraphs.text: Initial firefighting is limited to the workplace procedure and to trained personnel who have checked a safe escape route and equipment conditions. Power operation is also limited to what can be done from a safe, authorized position; do not approach the fire to switch it off. If flames or smoke spread, evacuate rather than persist in firefighting.

terms.meaning: Reporting an emergency fact to the designated recipient.
Fighting an early-stage fire within safe limits.
A marking showing the fire types and other conditions for which equipment may be used.
A route for leaving safely.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-058.activity:
4 minutes: Check the goal and terms.
10 minutes: Read the text and organize the conditions and reasons for decisions.
7 minutes: Separate the facts in the example from what remains unconfirmed.
7 minutes: For imaginary ordinary, oil and electrical fires, separate reporting and evacuation, suitability checks and prohibited actions.
2 minutes: Summarize the key points and what to confirm at work.
safety: Do not apply water to oil or energized parts, or approach smoke or the fire source to extinguish it.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-058.summary: Consider reporting and evacuation first. Initial firefighting requires suitable equipment, training and safe conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-059.title: Check handling, heat and chemical hazards by process
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-059.objective: Separate weight and travel-route checks, heat and dust hazards, exposure-control equipment and health checks.

paragraphs.title: Choose the method, not just whether you can lift it
paragraphs.text: For heavy objects, check weight, shape, gripping points, distance and route. Safety is not decided only by whether someone bends at the waist; ask about specified aids or team-handling methods. Do not force yourself to carry an unmanageable weight. Keep away from suspended loads and restricted areas.

paragraphs.title: Manage heat and dust separately
paragraphs.text: Areas near furnaces may involve heat stress; sand molds and polishing may involve dust. Check rest and hydration measures separately from source control, ventilation and protection. Report changes in physical condition early rather than enduring them. Follow workplace training and emergency procedures for the necessary response.

paragraphs.title: Connect labels, equipment and health
paragraphs.text: Before using a chemical, check its hazards, handling and emergency measures in the SDS. Use hoods and other exposure-control equipment in the specified condition, and check health-examination instructions too. Having had an examination is not a reason to switch off ventilation.

terms.meaning: The route along which people or objects move.
A hot environment that places heat stress on the body.
Being subjected to a harmful substance or similar hazard.
The part of equipment drawing in air near a source.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-059.activity:
4 minutes: Check the goal and terms.
10 minutes: Read the text and organize the conditions and reasons for decisions.
7 minutes: Separate the facts in the example from what remains unconfirmed.
7 minutes: Make an equipment, behavior and health checklist for three situations: a heavy object, a furnace area and a cleaning liquid.
2 minutes: Summarize the key points and what to confirm at work.
safety: Avoid forced lifting and contact with unknown substances. Do not turn off exposure-control equipment without authorization.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-059.summary: Choose measures for each process hazard. Health examinations and protective equipment do not replace engineering controls.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-060.title: Keep procedures readable and turn improvement ideas into formal changes
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-060.objective: Check access to procedures, their target and version, change approval and communication.

paragraphs.title: Information must be available when needed
paragraphs.text: A procedure states who does what, when and how. Merely possessing a document is insufficient if it cannot be read when needed at the work location. Check the equipment, product and version covered, and report failed displays or unreadable paper. Do not fill in unconfirmed conditions from memory alone.

paragraphs.title: An idea is not an approved change
paragraphs.text: Even if a step appears possible to shorten, do not change its order or conditions on the spot. Other processes’ quality or safety may be affected. Summarize the proposal’s purpose, expected benefit and possible adverse effects, then submit it through the company’s checks and approval.

paragraphs.title: Communication is required after approval
paragraphs.text: After a formal change, check when it takes effect, the target, separation from old versions, and whether training or notification is needed. Altering only your own paper does not inform the next operator. Check the location and update status of procedures at handover as well.

terms.meaning: Being able to consult necessary information.
An authorized person confirming that a change may be implemented.
Informing the people concerned.
The document version before a change.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-060.activity:
4 minutes: Check the goal and terms.
10 minutes: Read the text and organize the conditions and reasons for decisions.
7 minutes: Separate the facts in the example from what remains unconfirmed.
7 minutes: Draw the flow from an improvement proposal through approval, updating and communication. Write a report for an unreadable procedure.
2 minutes: Summarize the key points and what to confirm at work.
safety: Do not try an unapproved improvement on actual machinery or mix old and new versions.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-060.summary: Readable procedures and formal changes are necessary. Updates must include communication and checking applicability.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-061.title: Connect quality information across departments and QC circles
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-061.objective: Explain cooperation between design, procurement, manufacturing, inspection and shipping, and the role of small-group improvement.

paragraphs.title: Inspection is not the only department involved
paragraphs.text: Quality is supported by the whole flow: translating customer requirements into design, procuring materials, manufacturing, inspecting and shipping. When inspection finds the wrong material, do not assume it is only the inspector’s failure. Share information about instructions, identification and handovers as well.

paragraphs.title: A small team gathers facts
paragraphs.text: In a QC circle, a small workplace group discusses improvements to work quality and efficiency. Do not decide the cause by a majority vote alone; examine workplace facts and data. A proposal changing equipment or procedures still requires the specified approval.

paragraphs.title: Use PDCA for departmental handovers
paragraphs.text: For repeated incorrect labels, plan the goal and collection method, implement approved measures, compare results and feed them into further improvement. Do not declare completion only in the department taking action. Check that identification is also maintained by the receiving department.

terms.meaning: Obtaining necessary materials or items.
A team made up of a small number of people.
A workplace small-group activity improving quality and related matters.
Passing items or information to the next person responsible.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-061.activity:
4 minutes: Check the goal and terms.
10 minutes: Read the text and organize the conditions and reasons for decisions.
7 minutes: Separate the facts in the example from what remains unconfirmed.
7 minutes: For an imaginary labeling error, tabulate the facts each department supplies and the people checking each PDCA stage.
2 minutes: Summarize the key points and what to confirm at work.
safety: Do not use improvement activities as a reason to pass unjudged products onward or change procedures without approval.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-061.summary: Connect quality information between departments. QC circles also need facts, approval and checks of results.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-062.title: Make inspection-record errors and unjudged items traceable
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-062.objective: Ask about cases outside the criteria and errors in past records, and distinguish actual measurements from transcription.

paragraphs.title: Records represent work actually performed
paragraphs.text: Carry out inspection using approved criteria and procedures, and record results promptly. Even when results are usually identical, do not copy the last value without measuring. Link date and time, lot, instrument, value and judgment so the items represented by a result can be identified.

paragraphs.title: Ask about cases outside the criteria
paragraphs.text: Do not independently pass an item whose condition is absent from the procedure or difficult to judge. Keep unjudged items identified and separated, and tell the quality staff the target and uncertainty. A pass-rate goal does not permit relaxing the criteria.

paragraphs.title: Report errors even in someone else’s records
paragraphs.text: If an error is found in a past record, report it with the original record and affected target. Do not delete the history; obtain the prescribed correction and impact-scope checks. Also raise hard-to-perform or error-prone points to help prevent future mistakes.

terms.meaning: A condition where pass or fail has not yet been decided.
Copying information into another record.
Following the links between an item and its history.
Correcting a record error by the prescribed method.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-062.activity:
4 minutes: Check the goal and terms.
10 minutes: Read the text and organize the conditions and reasons for decisions.
7 minutes: Separate the facts in the example from what remains unconfirmed.
7 minutes: Using imaginary data, prepare a report of a record error and a separation label for unjudged items.
2 minutes: Summarize the key points and what to confirm at work.
safety: Do not delete records to conceal them or ship unjudged or nonconforming items without authorization.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-062.summary: Make records match the work performed. Report unjudged items and past errors in a traceable form.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-063.title: Read DC, AC and equipment ratings separately
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-063.objective: Explain differences in current direction and periodic change; do not select equipment from the voltage number alone.

paragraphs.title: Diagram the direction difference
paragraphs.text: Direct current flows in a consistent direction; alternating current changes direction periodically. Direction and voltage magnitude are separate matters. Both can be dangerous: DC does not mean there is no electric-shock hazard. Compare the directions using arrows and time diagrams on paper.

paragraphs.title: Equal voltage does not mean equal conditions
paragraphs.text: Numbers such as 100 V or 200 V alone do not identify DC or AC, frequency or equipment compatibility. Read the nameplate together with the specified supply and instructions. Do not connect equipment merely because the connector shape fits.

paragraphs.title: Withhold use when the supply is unknown
paragraphs.text: If a relocated machine’s supply marking is unreadable and only an old note remains, withhold connection. Report the machine number and marking condition, and confirm the appropriate ratings and connection. Keep actual energizing and wiring within the authorized work scope.

terms.meaning: Current flowing in a consistent direction.
Current changing direction periodically.
A voltage or other value permitted under specified conditions.
A plate displaying equipment identification, ratings and related information.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-063.activity:
4 minutes: Check the goal and terms.
10 minutes: Read the text and organize the conditions and reasons for decisions.
7 minutes: Separate the facts in the example from what remains unconfirmed.
7 minutes: Draw DC and AC direction diagrams, and use an imaginary nameplate to make fields for voltage, type and frequency.
2 minutes: Summarize the key points and what to confirm at work.
safety: Do not try connecting equipment with unclear markings or perform an energizing experiment.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-063.summary: Check current direction and ratings separately. Connector shape alone does not establish compatibility.
